articles.full_text:
Mumbai experienced sweltering conditions on Saturday afternoon, with residents braving the scorching heat as they went about their daily activities. According to the Maharashtra weather bulletin, Mumbai recorded a maximum temperature of 37 degrees Celsius, while the Santacruz weather station registered 37.8 degrees Celsius. (PICS/ SATEJ SHINDE)
01
The city's maximum temperature was 4.4 degrees above normal. Here is a look at how Mumbaikars navigated the heat on Saturday. (PICS/ SATEJ SHINDE)
02
Mumbai recorded a maximum temperature of 37 degrees Celsius on Friday, October 9, while the Santacruz weather station recorded 37.8 degrees Celsius, according to the Maharashtra weather bulletin
03
Mumbai's maximum temperature was 4.4 degrees above normal, while the minimum temperature stood at 27.1 degrees Celsius, 1.7 degrees above normal
04
Santacruz recorded a minimum temperature of 25.8 degrees Celsius. Across the Konkan region, Dahanu recorded a maximum of 36.9 degrees Celsius, followed by Ratnagiri at 36.7 degrees Celsius and Alibag at 34.9 degrees Celsius
05
No rainfall was recorded at Mumbai, Santacruz, Alibag, Ratnagiri and Dahanu
06
The wider Maharashtra weather data showed above-normal maximum temperatures across several regions. Amravati recorded the state's highest maximum temperature at 39.4 degrees Celsius, while Mahabaleshwar registered the lowest minimum temperature at 17.9 degrees Celsius.

Mumbai experienced its first post-monsoon heatwave on Friday, October 9, as the India Meteorological Department’s Santacruz observatory recorded a maximum temperature of 37.8 degrees Celsius, 4.7 degrees above normal. (Pic/Sayyed Sameer Abedi, Ashish Raje, Satej Shinde and Atul Kamble)
01
A man on a motorcycle is seen trying to shield himself from the scorching heat. Pic/Sayyed Sameer Abedi
02
Mumbai’s air quality improves to the satisfactory category- The city’s PM10 AQI stood at 99 on Friday, according to the Central Pollution Control Board, improving from Thursday’s reading of 120, which fell in the moderate category
03
An anticyclone contributes to Mumbai’s rising temperatures- IMD RMC Mumbai chief Bikram Singh attributed the warming to an anticyclone over Gujarat and adjoining North Maharashtra, while climatologist Rajesh Kapadia expected conditions to ease as the sea breeze returned
04
The IMD issues a yellow alert for hot and humid conditions- Greater Mumbai and neighbouring districts were placed under a yellow warning as above-normal temperatures continued following the withdrawal of the southwest monsoon
05
Mumbai records its highest October temperature in eight years- Friday’s maximum of 37.8 degree Celsius surpassed Thursday’s 37.6 degree Celsius reading at Santacruz, marking another day of unusually high temperatures after the monsoon withdrawal.
06
A fan provides relief to a woman at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus- With the mercury rising to 37.8 degree Celsius at Santacruz, commuters and people at public spaces looked for ways to stay cool amid the heatwave
07
A traffic police officer performs duty in Dadar amid the heat- The city’s soaring temperatures added to the challenge for people working outdoors, including traffic personnel managing vehicles under the afternoon sun
08
People watch cricket from the shade of a tree at Azad Maidan- With temperatures soaring across Mumbai, people sought shelter from the afternoon sun as the city experienced unusually hot October weather
09
An inter-school competition coach wears an umbrella hat at Azad Maidan- The coach gestures to players while using an umbrella hat for protection from the sun as Mumbai swelters under the post-monsoon heatwave
10
Pedestrians cool off with fresh fruit near the Gateway of India- Mumbai recorded its first post-monsoon heatwave on Friday, with the Santacruz observatory logging a maximum temperature of 37.8 degree Celsius 4.7 degrees above normal.

articles.title: Sidee faa'iidada shirkadda Samsung ay ugu korartay $80 bilyan oo doolar sanadkaan? - BBC

articles.full_text:
Shirkadda Samsung Electronics Co. waxay sheegtay inay filayso in faa'iidada rubuc-sannadeedka ay kor u kacdo ku dhawaad sagaal laab marka loo eego isla muddadaas sannadkii hore, taasoo ay keentay kororka baahida loo qabo jibka xusuusta ee loo isticmaalo xarumaha xogta garaadka macmalka ah.
Shirkadda tiknoolajiyadda ayaa ku qiyaastay in faa'iidada hawlgalka ay gaartay 107.4 tirilyan oo won ah (qiyaastii 61 bilyan oo ginni ama $80 bilyan) saddexdii bilood ee ugu dambeeyay dhammaadka Sebtembar. Tani waxay noqon doontaa rubuc-sannadeedkii afraad ee isku xiga ee Samsung ay ku soo saarto faa'iido rikoor ah.
Samsung waa mid ka mid ah shirkadaha ugu waaweyn ee adduunka ee xusuusta. Shirkadda SK Hynix ee Kuuriyada Koonfureed iyo Micron ee Mareykanka ayaa sidoo kale sameeya jibka xusuusta ee muhiimka u ah shirkadaha AI sida Nvidia.
Samsung, oo sidoo kale samaysa taleefannada casriga ah ee Galaxy Fold iyo S26, ayaa la filayaa inay faa'iido dheeraad ah ka hesho taleefannadeeda cusub ee la laabi karo; aaladaha waxaa la bilaabay bishii Agoosto.
Warbixinta maaliyadeed ee rubuc-saddexaad ee dhammaystiran ee Samsung ayaa la sii deyn doonaa dhammaadka Oktoobar.
Qaar ka mid ah shirkadaha waaweyn ee Kuuriyada Koonfureed ayaa bixinaya qiyaaso dakhli oo hordhac ah ka hor inta aysan sii deyn warbixinnadooda maaliyadeed oo dhammaystiran si ay u wargeliyaan maalgashadayaasha.
Qiyaasaha noocaas ah waxaa loo arkaa kuwo ka kalsooni badan kuwa falanqeeyayaasha dibadda, sababtoo ah waxay ku salaysan yihiin macluumaadka gudaha ee shirkadda.
Baahida adduunka oo dhan ee loo qabo jibka kombiyuutarka ee loo isticmaalo horumarinta AI ayaa cirka isku shareertay, taasoo kor u qaadaysa dakhliga iyo qiimaha saamiyada ee shirkadaha jibka tiknoolajiyada.
Warbixinada qotada dheer iyo wararka BBC Somali oo toos kuugu imanaaya WhatsApp.
Halkaan kaga soo biir
Dhamaadka xayeysiinta
Baahida sii kordheysa sannadihii u dambeeyay ayaa keentay yaraanta agabka semiconductor-ka adduunka oo dhan, taasoo kor u qaadaysa iibka shirkadaha sida Samsung. Qiimaha suuqa saamiyada ee Samsung ayaa kor u dhaafay $1 tiriliyan horraantii sanadkan.
Maalgashiga warshadaha ayaa sidoo kale si degdeg ah u kordhay. Shirkadaha waaweyn ee tignoolajiyada Mareykanka, sida Google, Amazon iyo Meta, ayaa ballan qaaday inay maalgelin doonaan in ka badan $650 bilyan oo mashaariicda AI ah sanadkan.
Bishii Juun, Kuuriyada Koonfureed waxay ku dhawaaqday qorshayaal qiimahoodu yahay ugu yaraan $880 bilyan oo loogu talagalay mashaariicda ay hoggaaminayaan Samsung iyo SK Hynix, oo loogu talagalay in lagu ballaariyo awoodda sameynta chips-ka dalka sanadaha soo socda.
Shirkadaha Aasiya ee iska soo horjeeda ee Japan, Shiinaha, iyo Taiwan ayaa sidoo kale si weyn u maalgashanaya warshadaha wax soo saarka chips-ka sababtoo ah baahida sii kordheysa ee AI.
Sababtoo ah yaraanta chips-ka iyo baahida sii kordheysa, Samsung iyo shirkado kale ayaa kor u qaadaya qiimaha alaabadooda, taasoo ka dhigaysa alaabada sida taleefannada casriga ah iyo kombiyuutarrada kuwo qaali ah.

articles.title: Red Alert: Delhi is militarised as millions mobilise against mass disenfranchisement - Progressive International

articles.full_text:
Statements
Statement from the Progressive International Observatory
We write from the barricades of Jantar Mantar, where the Government of India has deployed armed forces against citizens protesting mass disenfranchisement and defending their right to vote.Since 2025, more than 130 million names have been struck from India’s draft electoral rolls — an unprecedented project of disenfranchisement in the world’s largest democracy. Evidence suggests that it handed the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) an electoral advantage in several constituencies in recent state elections by removing voters from marginalised communities, including Muslim and Dalit voters.
Citizens from across the country are now in revolt. Today, 10 October, students, trade unionists and farmers are gathering in Delhi to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Their target is the “Special Intensive Revision” that struck those names from the rolls.
The government has reason to fear these students. The protest has been called by the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth movement whose first wave of protests in July ended with the resignation of the Education Minister, Dharmendra Pradhan.
In its second wave, the anger has spread far beyond student organisations — engulfing the country in a fight to defend the right to vote. Opposition parties from across the country, from the Indian National Congress to the Communist Party of India (Marxist), have stood on the front lines of this struggle. Hundreds of Members of Parliament marched in the streets to demand accountability, only to meet the same police crackdown. The Leader of the Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, was detained.
The Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls, launched in 2025 and presented as a clean-up of bad data, has become a purge of voters unwanted by the BJP. United Nations Special Rapporteurs have formally raised their concern with the Indian government over the removal of millions of names — and its impact on minorities.
Leaked documents now reveal that two of the three Election Commissioners objected on the record at least 14 times to Mr Kumar’s decisions regarding the revision of the rolls, warning that the move was illegal and unconstitutional, but were overridden. Mr Kumar was handpicked and appointed by a committee on which the government holds two of three votes.
The protesters’ demand is clear: the immediate resignation of Gyanesh Kumar and a rollback of the Special Intensive Revision.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government has answered the call to protest with a siege of the capital.
Some 26,000 armed paramilitary personnel and 20,000 police have been deployed to Delhi. Buses and trains bound for the city have been searched, and students suspected of travelling to the protest have been pre-emptively detained. Metro stations have been closed. Trains into Delhi have been cancelled. An internet shutdown has been announced.
On 2 October, the anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi’s birth, protesters took to the streets of Delhi and Mumbai in non-violent disobedience — and were met with paramilitary cordons and anti-riot vehicles. Roads to Jantar Mantar, Delhi’s designated protest site, were barricaded.
Mass detentions followed, and again the next day. Students were forced onto buses, and many say they were beaten and harassed. On 6 October, police turned on students and opposition leaders once more.
The world is watching. From on the ground in Delhi, the Progressive International Observatory calls on progressive forces around the world to demand that the Government of India withdraw its forces from Delhi, conduct an independent investigation into the Election Commission of India, and roll back the revision.
Each time, the protesters have returned.
